abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) expand language models to process and interpret audio, but also expose them to heterogeneous audio jailbreaks. We ask whether successful jailbreaks reflect failures to recognize harmful intent or failures occurring after such recognition. Layer-wise probing reveals the latter: risk-related information remains decodable from intermediate representations, yet the internal risk signal fails to translate into refusal in later-layer processing. We identify this discrepancy as the risk-to-refusal gap. Building on this finding, we propose AEGIS, a detect-then-intervene defense whose mid-layer risk gate selectively activates downstream safety adapters. Across six LALMs and three heterogeneous audio jailbreak benchmarks, AEGIS reduces the average unsafe rate from 17.9% to 0.4%, while causing only a marginal increase in over-refusal on benign inputs. These results establish selective internal intervention as an effective path toward more robust refusal in LALMs. The code is available at this https URL.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文追问音频越狱成功是认不出有害意图还是认出后未触发拒绝，用逐层探测定位到后者并提出中层风险门控加后层安全适配的先检测后干预方法，在六个大音频语言模型和三类异构音频越狱上把平均不安全率从 17.9% 降到 0.4%，代价是良性过拒绝平均上升 6.3 个百分点。
originalTitle: AEGIS: Audio Endogenous Guarding via Internal Signals Against Large Audio-Language Model Jailbreaks
readerTitle: 能识别风险却不拒绝：音频越狱暴露的识别与拒答脱节及选择性内部干预
